resources.name: Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary
resources.license_or_access_notes: Official Notre Dame academic distribution is public; review terms before vendoring dictionary files.
resources.why_fit: Best fit for deterministic finance-language extension, especially uncertainty, modal strength, and constraint cues that can stay auditable.
resources.why_not: Dictionary counts still need conversational context and do not solve dialogue structure or multi-domain review on their own.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Extend canonical deterministic finance lexicons and benchmark transcript-only feature coverage.
resources.notes: Strongest immediate fit for earnings-call terminology without adding model dependencies.

resources.name: Financial PhraseBank
resources.license_or_access_notes: Original paper is public; mirrors often expose separate dataset terms, so reuse should be re-checked before local benchmarking.
resources.why_fit: Useful small finance benchmark for sanity-checking sentiment behavior on short financial text.
resources.why_not: Short headline sentiment does not map cleanly to transcript evidence, analyst pressure, or reviewer actionability.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Benchmark-only transcript sanity checks for finance sentiment, not canonical scoring.
resources.notes: Helpful evaluation reference, but weaker fit than transcript-specific lexicon work.

resources.name: Switchboard Dialog Act Corpus / MRDA
resources.license_or_access_notes: Core corpora are gated through LDC or research distribution; metadata and papers are accessible.
resources.why_fit: Strong conceptual fit for question-answer structure, interruptions, and conversational move taxonomies.
resources.why_not: Access is gated and the domains are not earnings, support, or sales, so direct adoption would add friction.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Dialogue-act taxonomy reference and later benchmark-only experiments if access becomes available.
resources.notes: Good methodology reference, but not a default-path dependency.

resources.name: FinBERT
resources.license_or_access_notes: Model card is public; downstream commercial and data-provenance review is still advisable before broader use.
resources.why_fit: Good optional finance-domain comparison point for transcript sentiment benchmarking.
resources.why_not: Black-box sentiment scores are too narrow and too opaque to become canonical signal extraction in this repo.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Optional benchmark-only comparator for finance text, especially earnings-call phrasing.
resources.notes: Useful as a measured comparator, not as product truth.

resources.name: openSMILE
resources.license_or_access_notes: audEERING documents research-oriented usage; commercial usage requires care.
resources.why_fit: Strong bounded fit for pauses, energy, and prosodic review cues without claiming hidden-state inference.
resources.why_not: Audio features add dependency and rights complexity and should not be interpreted as internal-state truth.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Optional audio adapter for sparse prosody cues in later pilot cases.
resources.notes: Only useful once aligned approved audio exists.

resources.name: MELD
resources.license_or_access_notes: Public project resources exist, but media provenance and downstream reuse posture should be treated carefully.
resources.why_fit: Useful research reference for multimodal conversation emotion benchmarks and evaluation language.
resources.why_not: Friends-based emotion labels are a weak fit for enterprise transcript review and recruiter-facing proof.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Benchmark framing only for future multimodal comparisons, not core pipeline work.
resources.notes: Keep this in documentation until aligned business-conversation media exists.

resources.name: OpenCV
resources.license_or_access_notes: OpenCV 4.5.0+ is Apache 2.0; older versions are BSD-licensed.
resources.why_fit: Lightweight fit for frame stats, motion proxies, and simple video preprocessing if sparse visual review is added later.
resources.why_not: Basic vision utilities do not justify body-language certainty claims and are far from canonical transcript evaluation.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Optional video utility layer for later sparse cue extraction only.
resources.notes: Best treated as infrastructure, not as inference evidence on its own.

resources.name: CMU-MOSEI
resources.license_or_access_notes: Widely cited research benchmark, but current practical access/download path should be re-verified before use.
resources.why_fit: Only useful as a broad multimodal sentiment benchmark reference.
resources.why_not: Generic multimodal sentiment/emotion is a poor fit for transcript-first, evidence-backed business signal extraction.
resources.best_use_in_signal_engine: Documentation-only cautionary reference for later multimodal benchmarking decisions.
resources.notes: Low portfolio fit for the current repo direction.
